field.allow_private_help: By default only public addresses are reached, so that a webhook cannot probe your network. Turn it on for a receiver on this machine or on your network.
field.body_help: Leave it empty to post the note as JSON. For another format, write the body as a Go template: '{{.subject}}', '{{.title}}', '{{.text}}', '{{.link}}', '{{.event}}', '{{.time}}' and '{{.data}}' hold what the JSON does; '{{json .text}}' writes a value as JSON, '{{urlquery .text}}' for a form. For example: '{"msgtype": "text", "text": {"content": {{json .text}}}}'
field.content_type_help: The Content-Type of a body made from the template, such as application/x-www-form-urlencoded for a form.
field.deploy_body_help: Leave it empty to post the certificate as JSON. To call an API that takes another format, write the body as a Go template with the fields of that JSON: '{{.domains}}', '{{.fullchain}}', '{{.cert}}', '{{.chain}}', '{{.privkey}}', '{{.not_after}}' and the like; '{{json .fullchain}}' writes a value as JSON, '{{index .domains 0}}' is the primary domain. For example: '{"cert": {{json .fullchain}}, "key": {{json .privkey}}}'
field.deploy_url_help: Must be an https:// address, as the requests carry the private key. The endpoint may answer '{"ref": "…"}', which JEC passes back in previous with the next deployment, so that the old certificate can go.
field.headers_help: One per line, such as Authorization: Bearer xxx. Not shown again once saved.
field.secret_help: When set, each request carries X-JEC-Signature: sha256= and the HMAC-SHA256 of the body with this secret, so the receiver can tell it comes from JEC.
field.url_help: JEC sends it POST requests with JSON bodies.
